monuments.name: Flinders Street Station (1910 Copper Dome & Entrance Clocks)
monuments.localName: Flinders Street Railway Station ("Under the Clocks")
monuments.architect: Fawcett & Ashworth French Renaissance Copper Dome, Clock Tower & Yellow-and-Blood-Red Facade
monuments.architecturalStyle: Fawcett & Ashworth French Renaissance Copper Dome, Clock Tower & Yellow-and-Blood-Red Facade
monuments.fact: Opened on September 12, 1854 as Melbourne Terminus for Australia’s first steam railway and rebuilt in 1905–1910 with its iconic bronze-green dome, Elizabeth Street clock tower, and nine departure indicator clocks.

monuments.name: Royal Exhibition Building (1880 UNESCO World Heritage Dome)
monuments.architect: Joseph Reed Florentine Duomo Octagonal Dome, Cruciform Great Hall & Triumphal Fanlight Portals
monuments.architecturalStyle: Joseph Reed Florentine Duomo Octagonal Dome, Cruciform Great Hall & Triumphal Fanlight Portals
monuments.fact: Designed by Joseph Reed for the 1880 Melbourne International Exhibition with a 68m octagonal dome inspired by Brunelleschi’s Florence Cathedral, it hosted the opening of the first Parliament of Australia on May 9, 1901.

monuments.name: Shrine of Remembrance (1934 Stepped Pyramid Mausoleum)
monuments.architect: Hudson & Wardrop Parthenon Doric Portico & Stepped Pyramid of Halicarnassus
monuments.architecturalStyle: Hudson & Wardrop Parthenon Doric Portico & Stepped Pyramid of Halicarnassus
monuments.fact: Designed by WWI veterans Phillip Hudson and James Wardrop in Tynong granite, its roof aperture is calibrated so a beam of sunlight sweeps across the word "LOVE" on the Stone of Remembrance at 11 a.m. every November 11.

monuments.name: Federation Square (2002 Deconstructivist Pinwheel Facades)
monuments.architect: Lab Architecture Studio Kimberley Sandstone, Perforated Zinc & Glass Pinwheel Fractals over Rail Deck
monuments.architecturalStyle: Lab Architecture Studio Kimberley Sandstone, Perforated Zinc & Glass Pinwheel Fractals over Rail Deck
monuments.fact: Built on a massive structural deck bridging the Jolimont railyards opposite Flinders Street Station, Federation Square’s facade is tiled from 475,000 Kimberley sandstone cobbles and five self-similar "pinwheel" triangles.

monuments.name: Eureka Tower & Melbourne Skydeck (2006 24-Carat Gold Crown)
monuments.architect: Fender Katsalidis Cobalt-Blue Glass, 24-Carat Gold-Plated Top 10 Floors, Red Blood Stripe & Cantilevered Edge Cube
monuments.architecturalStyle: Fender Katsalidis Cobalt-Blue Glass, 24-Carat Gold-Plated Top 10 Floors, Red Blood Stripe & Cantilevered Edge Cube
monuments.fact: Designed by Fender Katsalidis to commemorate the 1854 Victorian Gold Rush Eureka Stockade rebellion—combining a cobalt-blue and white stockade flag facade, a vertical crimson stripe, and 3,680 panes of 24-carat gold-plated glass on levels 83–92.

monuments.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground — The ’G (100,024-Seat Colosseum)
monuments.architect: Circular 100,024-Seat Grandstand Bowl & Six 85m Tubular Steel Light Towers (1985)
monuments.architecturalStyle: Circular 100,024-Seat Grandstand Bowl & Six 85m Tubular Steel Light Towers (1985)
monuments.fact: Founded in 1853, birthplace of Australian Rules Football (1859) and Test Cricket (1877), main stadium of the 1956 Melbourne Olympics, and largest stadium in the Southern Hemisphere with six 85-meter light towers.

monuments.name: Arts Centre Melbourne & 162m Ballerina Spire
monuments.architect: 162m White Steel Space-Frame Spire & Cascading Ballerina Tutu Mesh Skirt
monuments.architecturalStyle: 162m White Steel Space-Frame Spire & Cascading Ballerina Tutu Mesh Skirt
monuments.fact: Because waterlogged Yarra River silt prevented building high theater fly-towers above ground, architect Sir Roy Grounds sank the State Theatre five levels underground and crowned the roof with a 162-meter lattice spire.

monuments.name: Bolte Bridge (1999 Twin 140m Silver Needle Towers)
monuments.architect: Balanced Cantilever Box-Girder Viaduct & Twin 140m Tapering Silver Concrete Obelisks
monuments.architecturalStyle: Balanced Cantilever Box-Girder Viaduct & Twin 140m Tapering Silver Concrete Obelisks
monuments.fact: Designed by Melbourne architects Denton Corker Marshall as the western gateway to the city, its two 140-meter tapering silver concrete needles rise without structural cables on either side of the Yarra River deck.
